Early Modern English (sometimes abbreviated EModE [ 1 ] or EMnE ), also known as Early New English ( ENE ), and colloquially Shakespeare's English , Shakespearean English , or King James' English , is the stage of the English language from the beginning of the Tudor period to the English Interregnum and Restoration , or from the transition from Middle English , in the late 15th century, to the transition to Modern English , in the mid-to-late 17th century. [ 2 ]
